text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

After making it to the Federal Government's short-list in October with Auckland International Airport, property giant Westfield Holdings Ltd has quit the A$2.5 billion first stage of the airports privatisation, choosing to concentrate resources on developents with the core business in the US, Australia and Asia. Page 2.

The Victorian and South Australian Governments and the car industry have attacked the Industry Commission's majority report on the car industry, with South Australian Premier John Olsen calling the report a "potential disaster for South Australia" and Vicorian Industry Minister Mark Birrell saying its recommendations would lead to Australian job cuts and the stunting of long-term industry growth. Ford Australia president David Morgan said the report's primary focus on tariffs made it a "simplistic treatmnt of a complex subject". Page 4.

Optus Communications chief executive Ziggy Switkowski said yesterday the group had ruled out its A$4.5 billion stock exchange listing before resolving its court battle with the Seven Network, which begins in February, but it was still possible that a prospectus might be issued before a settlement. Page 21.

Entertainer and lawyer Steve Vizard has approached several institutions and brokers about the possibility of a float of his television production house, Artists Services. Broking houses Were Stockbroking and Burden Buckeridge and Young said there would be strong interest in a listing of the production house, given the recent interest in entertainment companies listed on the Australian Stock Exchange. Page 21.

CanWest Global Communications head Izzy Apser said yesterday 6.45 percent stakeholder in the Ten Network, the AMP Society, had jeopardised plans for a speedy listing of the network by calling for a "simple" float of Ten and labelling other shareholders' plans as the second best option. Page 22.

The A$215 million south-west Queensland gas pipeline has been completed and is ready to begin deliveries to the State's rapidly growing east coast market. Deliveries of Cooper Basin gas from the State's south-west corner will begin by January 1. Page 23.
THE AUSTRALIAN

WMC Ltd has launched its long-awaited assault on the international fertiliser market after it announced plans to develop a A$650 million phosphate fertiliser project at its Duchess-Phosphate Hill deposit near Mt Isa, Queensland. By 1999 WMC plans to produce one million tonnes a year of high analysis ammonium phosphate fertilisers from the estimated two billion tonne resource. Page 21

A partial float of broadcaster the Ten Group Ltd has strengthened as major shareholder Telecasters North Queensland indicated that it would join CanWest Global Communications Inc's proposed unit trust. CanWest, another major player in Ten, is believed to ave put forward the idea of the listed unit trust to reduce its economic interest from 76 per cent to 57.5 per cent to appease the Australian Broadcasting Authority's media ownership regulations. Page 21.

Foster's Brewing Group shares inched up a further two per cents yesterday as speculation continued over the future of mining giant BHP's 37 percent share in the brewer. Over the past week Foster's shares have increased by 10 per cent as the market has beome convinced that Foster's has convinced BHP to unload its unwanted holding. Page 22

Qantas Airways has come through on a promise to shareholders to shed under-performing routes with yesterday's announcement of new schedules. The carrier is set to cut flights between Brisbane and Taipei and a direct flight from Melbourne to Japan. However, Qantas is aiming to expand its role across Asia and also into New Zealand. Page 23.

Don Bourke, the chairman of the Federal Government's private venture capital arm, Australian Technology Group Ltd, has warned that the economy was under threat of sliding further behind its major competitors unless policy was implemented which will overse the severe drought of venture capital. Bourke claimed that the limited success in bringing new technologies to the market reflected Australia's shortage of venture capital for new companies. Page 23.

The Victorian Employers Chamber of Commerce has demanded that the Kennett Government implement tax cuts in its next Budget to kick-start the State's "very sluggish" economy. The peak business group highlighted that industry and business in Victoria were sill paying about 10 per cent more tax than the Australian State average. Page 23.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

The prospect of a legal challenge to St George Bank's A$2.65 billion takeover offer for Advance Bank has decreased ahead of Monday's Advance shareholders' meeting. A legal challenge was foreshadowed by National Australia Bank's chief executive, Don Argus,after NAB took out a three per cent stake in Advance and claimed the takeover was "ineffective in law". Although the proposal for a legal challenge has waned, the Australian Securities Commission has now voiced "concerns" about the takeover deal after NAB supplied the ASC with legal opinion over the takeover offer. Page 25.

Although Pacific Dunlop has confirmed that it would expect a poor first-half profit, share prices have remained high amid speculation that a multi-billion-dollar predator was lurking in the wings. Nonetheless, PacDun remains committed that its full-year rofits would be higher than last year's A$162 million result. Shares in the retail and production giant closed yesterday three cents higher at A$3.07. Page 25.

WMC has announced that it will spend A$650 million developing one of the world's largest fertiliser resources at Phosphate Hill in north-west Queensland. WMC's managing director, Hugh Morgan, said the project would improve Australia's balance of payment's by A$350 million and A$400 million when full production is reached in 1999. Page 25.

After publicly expressing concern about CanWest Global Communications' proposal to float the Ten Network, the AMP Society has been called to appear before the Australian Broadcasting Authority to give evidence to its investigation into the level of control CanWest has over Ten. Page 27.

Ridley Corp warned yesterday that its December half-year profit is expected to drop 10 percent because of weaker prices for stockfeed and lower sales of live cattle. Ridley is expected to achieve a net profit for the full year to June 30, 1997, of A$21 million compared with the A$22.4 million earned last year. Page 27.

MLC has sold a 40 per cent stake in Sydney's MLC Centre for A$172 million, with General Property Trust increasing its holding in the MLC Centre to 35 per cent and Queensland Investment Corp taking a 25 per cent stake. The deal allows GPT and QIC to move to 50 per cent ownership of the centre by July next year. Page 27.
THE AGE

WMC yesterday gave the green light for the A$650 million development of its Queensland fertiliser project, in a move that will underpin the group's growth into the next century, along with other projects including, the A$1.25 billion expansion of the Olymic Dam mine and the A$157 million expansion of the St Ives gold operation near Kalgoorlie. Page C1.

Sources at Advance Bank have revealed that National Australia Bank has secured at least three percent, but not more than five percent of the shares of Advance as part of a plan to stop the bank's merger with St George with a legal challenge. The NAB purchases were made in early November and Advance has not noticed any other unusual activity since then. Page C1.

In two very different views on the needs of the car industry, the majority report of the Productivity Commission, signed by Bill Scales and Jeffrey Rae, has concluded that the Australian car industry would thrive and become more internationally competitive without most of its protection, while the minority report of Ian Webber called the proposed tariff cuts "folly", leading to an industry that would be neither "sustainable" nor "prosperous". Page C1.

National Rail managing director Vince Graham said yesterday the Government-owned rail freight operator might buy some of the privatised Australian National train group. The Federal Government announced plans to privatise Australian National next year and also to sell its 40 per cent stake in National Rail. Page C3.

Ballarat Brewing has lifted its interim net profit form A$1.33 million to A$1.8 million after a 61 per cent rise in revenue. The result was boosted by hotel trading revenues, which more than doubled from A$2.87 million to A$7.38 million. Page C3.

Telecasters North Queensland, which holds a 20 per cent economic interest and 40 per cent voting stake in the Ten Group, said yesterday it had no discussions with CanWest Global Communications on a float of the Ten Group and intended to go ahead with its plan to become a pure investment vehicle in Ten. Page C3.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
